statement: Over C let H be the 7-dimensional subspace of all 4x4 Hankel matrices H_ij=s_(i+j). For EVERY V in M4(C), span(H,V) is spanned by matrices of rank at most 2. The statement remains true after any fixed invertible left/right local transformations of H and V. Thus adjoining one arbitrary pure vector to any positive state whose range is a local-invertible image of H cannot produce a range-criterion proof of Schmidt number at least 3. This DOES NOT assert that any such state has Schmidt number at most 2.
fresh_public_source_and_scope: The actual public construction in Johnston-Lovitz, arXiv:2609.11849v1, sections 1.2, 2.1 and 2.3 (https://arxiv.org/html/2609.11849v1), takes sigma_4,4 to be the normalized projector onto the fully symmetric six-qubit subspace expressed in two three-qubit Dicke bases, then adds one pure vector. Its seven basis matrices have entries sqrt(binomial(3,i)binomial(3,j)/binomial(6,i+j)) on a fixed anti-diagonal, so their span is D H D with D=diag(1,sqrt(3),sqrt(3),1). Hence the displayed all-V theorem applies to every one-vector perturbation of this base, independently of the selected vector or perturbation weight. The cited paper's dimension argument gives only SN>=2 in 4x4; the present statement is not claimed to occur there, and is a range-only obstruction, not an upper bound on Schmidt number. This is fresh public-source use under the later frontier-first ruling, not a reconstruction of the separately stopped old JL audit or any held selected-parameter episode or consumer.
geometry_imports: The first secant variety of the degree-six rational normal curve is precisely the projective rank<=2 locus of the 4x4 middle Hankel catalecticant; its ideal is generated by the 3x3 catalecticant minors. In particular it is irreducible and three-dimensional. Import: Raicu, Secant Varieties of Segre-Veronese Varieties (2011), https://academicweb.nd.edu/~craicu/thesis.pdf, introduction section 1.3, especially the n=2 catalecticant case. Also import the standard projective dimension theorem, preservation of Hilbert function by weighted initial ideals, the degree of a proper linear section with local intersection multiplicities, and the Thom-Porteous determinantal class formula. None is a formal-verification claim.
preliminaries: Let X be the projective variety of rank<=2 4x4 matrices in P^15. It is irreducible of dimension 11 and degree 20. Its class is c2^2-c1*c3=10^2-4*20=20, using c((O)^4-(O(-1))^4)=(1-h)^(-4). Let Z=X intersect P(H); by the cited secant identity, Z is irreducible of dimension 3. Its degree is at most 10: give s_k weight k^2. Each of the sixteen 3x3 Hankel minors has a unique largest-weight monomial, its diagonal product. The distinct products are exactly s_i s_j s_k with 0<=i<j<k<=6 and successive gaps at least 2. The associated squarefree monomial ideal has exactly ten 4-element maximal-dimensional faces and no 5-element face, so its quotient has dimension 4 and degree 10. Since it is contained in the initial ideal of Z's minor ideal, Hilbert-function comparison gives deg(Z)<=10. The checker independently establishes all finite monomial and face counts; no assertion that those minors form a Groebner basis is needed.
symmetric_direction_case: If V is symmetric and outside H, E=span(H,V) is an 8-dimensional subspace of the 10-dimensional symmetric matrices. The projective symmetric rank<=2 variety has dimension 6 in P^9: write a generic matrix as BB^T with B 4x2, quotienting the 1-dimensional complex orthogonal action. Thus every nonempty component of P(E) intersect this variety has dimension at least 7+6-9=4. Since its intersection with P(H) is Z of dimension 3, there is a rank<=2 point outside P(H).
nonsymmetric_direction_case: Let V-V^T be nonzero. At a rank-two Hankel matrix H(z,w)=u(z)u(z)^T+u(w)u(w)^T, u(t)=(1,t,t^2,t^3)^T and z!=w, put s=z+w, p=zw, k1=(p,-s,1,0)^T, k2=(0,p,-s,1)^T and K=[k1 k2]. Both vectors annihilate u(z),u(w), and the tangent space of X at H(z,w) is {M: K^T M K=0}. The image of H under M->K^T M K is all Sym_2: for Hankel u(t)u(t)^T the image is (t-z)^2(t-w)^2 [[1,t],[t,t^2]], and three distinct t values span Sym_2. The skew part supplied by V is k1^T(V-V^T)k2 = A01 p^2-A02 p*s+A03 p+A12(s^2-p)-A13 s+A23, where A=V-V^T. The six coefficient polynomials are linearly independent; the integer checker verifies determinant 1 of their coefficient matrix. Since A!=0, the expression is nonzero for generic z,w, and hence span(H,V)+T_H X fills all 16 matrix dimensions at at least one such point. Although the displayed equal-weight two-parameter family is not itself dense in Z, transversality is an open condition on the irreducible Z; a single transverse point gives generic transversality there, and the component Z has local intersection multiplicity 1.
degree_conclusion: Suppose no rank<=2 point of P(E) lies outside P(H). Then the entire set X intersect P(E) is the irreducible Z, with expected dimension 3. The linear section is proper, so its intersection cycle has degree deg(X)=20. Transversality makes its sole component Z occur with multiplicity 1, so its degree would be deg(Z)<=10, a contradiction. Thus an outside rank<=2 matrix exists for every nonsymmetric V as well.
span_conclusion: H itself is spanned by rank-one matrices u(t)u(t)^T: any seven distinct t give an invertible 7x7 Vandermonde matrix on the anti-diagonal coordinates. If V is already in H this suffices; otherwise one additional rank<=2 point outside H found above, together with those rank-one matrices, spans all of E. Local invertible transformations preserve matrix rank.

exact_check.observed: Integer arithmetic independently generates all sixteen Hankel minors, checks the unique weighted diagonal leading monomial, identifies 10 distinct squarefree generators, counts 10 four-element faces and zero five-element faces, verifies determinant 1 of the six wedge coefficient vectors, and evaluates the Porteous integer 20. It does not prove the named algebraic-geometry imports or the written transversality/degree argument.

limits: A universal range-span result for one seven-dimensional support and its one-vector extensions, not a Schmidt-number decomposition, PPT witness, target solution, novelty clearance, formal proof, or external review. WRITTEN with named algebraic-geometry imports and exact integer/rational checks.
